# Daemon notice IDs need a protected dedupe namespace

<a id="body"></a>

## Body

Origin-aware deduplication does not protect daemon intent from other local senders. FYIs are keyed by (origin, id), not sender/recipient. Ordinary local messages and daemon notices share the empty origin. INSERT OR IGNORE can therefore drop the daemon's different message while hold_fyi still reports Held.

Before adding predictable internal notification IDs, try an ordinary caller sending as itself to another recipient with the future daemon ID. A persisted once-per-occurrence mark can then turn the collision into permanent suppression of that notice and a false Held audit. No victim identity assertion is required, so this is not C32's F88-only residual.

Use a daemon-controlled namespace or an unguessable occurrence identity unavailable before admission. A deduplicated row from a different sender/recipient is not admission of the intended notice. Test adversarial preoccupation, honest repeated delivery and restart recovery separately; Held remains admission, never model completion.
